name: Southpoint Tower
summary: Forsaken scouts watch the Alliance from Southpoint Tower, near Hillsbrad's western edge. The ruined Lordaeron post overlooks the road into Silverpine Forest.

sections.title: A Ruined Sentinel
sections.body: Southpoint Tower overlooks the highway between Silverpine Forest and Hillsbrad Foothills. The Kingdom of Lordaeron built it to guard the way between the eastern farmlands and the western woods. After the Third War and the Scourge's destruction of the kingdom, the stonework fell into ruin. Now the tower is roofless and crumbling, a remnant of human rule in fractured lands.

sections.title: Eyes on the Hills
sections.body: Forsaken agents watch Alliance patrols from the ruined tower. Deathstalker Lesh is stationed there, watching nearby human settlements in Hillsbrad Fields and travelers on the main road. Though its walls have fallen, the tower's vantage remains valuable. So near hostile territory, this lonely post often becomes a flashpoint for skirmishes.

faq.answer: Southpoint Tower stands at Hillsbrad Foothills' western edge, just south of the road into Silverpine Forest and west of Hillsbrad Fields.

faq.q: Who controls Southpoint Tower right now?
faq.answer: The Forsaken control Southpoint Tower. Deathstalker Lesh watches the road and nearby Alliance forces from its ruined walls.

faq.q: Why is the tower in ruins?
faq.answer: During Lordaeron's fall, the Scourge ravaged the region and battered the tower, forcing its abandonment. No one has repaired it, and only broken stone walls remain.

faq.q: Why do Alliance players attack this outpost?
faq.answer: Alliance travelers attack because a Forsaken scout watches human territory from the isolated post near the border. Its position makes it a tempting target for travelers between Southshore and the western roads.

angles.text: As Forsaken, you can watch human troop movements out of Hillsbrad from this perch near the Silverpine border.
As an Alliance scout, you can target the ruined tower, where an enemy spy watches the road to Silverpine and Hillsbrad's human settlements.
